# dsaupd

> Reverse communication interface for the Implicitly Restarted Lanczos iteration.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dsaupd from '@rreusser/blahpack/arpack/base/dsaupd';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dsaupd(
    order,
    state,
    ido,
    bmat,
    N,
    which,
    nev, tol,
    resid, strideResid,
    ncv,
    V, LDV,
    iparam, strideIparam,
    ipntr, strideIpntr,
    workd,
    workl,
    lworkl,
    infoIn
) → integer
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | in |  | one of `'row-major'`, `'column-major'` | storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `state` | `Object` | in/out |  |  | persistent reverse-communication state (pass `{}` on first use) |
| `ido` | `Int32Array` | in/out |  |  | reverse-communication flag (length-1; in/out) |
| `bmat` | `("standard"\|"generalized")` | in |  |  | `'standard'` or `'generalized'` eigenproblem |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | order of the problem |
| `which` | `("LM"\|"SM"\|"LA"\|"SA"\|"BE")` | in |  |  | which eigenvalues to compute (`'LM'`, `'SM'`, `'LA'`, `'SA'`, `'BE'`) |
| `nev` | `integer` | in |  |  | number of eigenvalues to compute |
| `tol` | `number` | in |  |  | relative accuracy for Ritz value convergence |
| `resid` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `N` |  | residual vector (length N; in/out) |
| ↳ `strideResid` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `resid` |
| `ncv` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | number of Lanczos vectors (columns of `V`) |
| `V` | `Float64Array` | out | `null × ncv` |  | Lanczos basis (N-by-ncv, column-major; out) |
| ↳ `LDV` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  |  | leading dimension of `V` |
| `iparam` | `Int32Array` | in/out | `11` |  | input/output parameters (length 11; in/out) |
| ↳ `strideIparam` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `iparam` |
| `ipntr` | `Int32Array` | out | `11` |  | workspace pointers (length 11; out) |
| ↳ `strideIpntr` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `ipntr` |
| `workd` | `(Float64Array\|null)` | in/out | `≥ 3 * N` |  | reverse-communication workspace (length >= 3*N) |
| `workl` | `(Float64Array\|null)` | in/out |  |  | private workspace (length >= ncv^2 + 8*ncv) |
| `lworkl` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | length of `workl` |
| `infoIn` | `integer` | in/out |  |  | nonzero on the first call to signal a user-supplied initial residual |

**Returns** `integer`: INFO

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` fourth argument must be one of the following: "standard", "generalized"
- `TypeError` sixth argument must be one of the following: "LM", "SM", "LA", "SA", "BE"
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` workd array must have sufficient length
- `RangeError` workl array must have sufficient length

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dsaupd.ndarray(
    state,
    ido,
    bmat,
    N,
    which,
    nev, tol,
    resid, strideResid, offsetResid,
    ncv,
    V, strideV1, strideV2, offsetV,
    iparam, strideIparam, offsetIparam,
    ipntr, strideIpntr, offsetIpntr,
    workd, strideWorkd, offsetWorkd,
    workl, strideWorkl, offsetWorkl,
    lworkl,
    infoIn
) → integer
```

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `state` | `Object` | in/out |  |  | persistent reverse-communication state (pass `{}` on first use) |
| `ido` | `Int32Array` | in/out |  |  | reverse-communication flag (length-1; in/out) |
| `bmat` | `("standard"\|"generalized")` | in |  |  | `'standard'` or `'generalized'` eigenproblem |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | order of the problem |
| `which` | `("LM"\|"SM"\|"LA"\|"SA"\|"BE")` | in |  |  | which eigenvalues to compute (`'LM'`, `'SM'`, `'LA'`, `'SA'`, `'BE'`) |
| `nev` | `integer` | in |  |  | number of eigenvalues to compute |
| `tol` | `number` | in |  |  | relative accuracy for Ritz value convergence |
| `resid` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `N` |  | residual vector (length N; in/out) |
| ↳ `strideResid` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `resid` |
| ↳ `offsetResid` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `resid` |
| `ncv` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | number of Lanczos vectors (columns of `V`) |
| `V` | `Float64Array` | out | `null × ncv` |  | Lanczos basis (N-by-ncv, column-major; out) |
| ↳ `strideV1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first (row) dimension of `V` |
| ↳ `strideV2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second (column) dimension of `V` |
| ↳ `offsetV` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `V` |
| `iparam` | `Int32Array` | in/out | `11` |  | input/output parameters (length 11; in/out) |
| ↳ `strideIparam` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `iparam` |
| ↳ `offsetIparam` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `iparam` |
| `ipntr` | `Int32Array` | out | `11` |  | workspace pointers (length 11; out) |
| ↳ `strideIpntr` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `ipntr` |
| ↳ `offsetIpntr` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `ipntr` |
| `workd` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `≥ 3 * N` |  | reverse-communication workspace (length >= 3*N) |
| ↳ `strideWorkd` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `workd` |
| ↳ `offsetWorkd` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `workd` |
| `workl` | `Float64Array` | in/out |  |  | private workspace (length >= ncv^2 + 8*ncv) |
| ↳ `strideWorkl` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `workl` |
| ↳ `offsetWorkl` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `workl` |
| `lworkl` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | length of `workl` |
| `infoIn` | `integer` | in/out |  |  | nonzero on the first call to signal a user-supplied initial residual |

**Returns** `integer`: INFO

**Throws**

- `TypeError` third argument must be one of the following: "standard", "generalized"
- `TypeError` fifth argument must be one of the following: "LM", "SM", "LA", "SA", "BE"
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` workd array must have sufficient length
- `RangeError` workl array must have sufficient length

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`.

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Int32Array from '@stdlib/array/int32/lib/index.js';
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import dsaupd from '@rreusser/blahpack/arpack/base/dsaupd';

// Compute the 3 largest eigenvalues of the 10x10 1-D Laplacian (OP = A, B = I):
const n = 10;
const A = new Float64Array( n * n );
let i;
for ( i = 0; i < n; i++ ) {
	A[ i + ( i * n ) ] = 2.0;
	if ( i < n - 1 ) {
		A[ i + ( ( i + 1 ) * n ) ] = -1.0;
		A[ ( i + 1 ) + ( i * n ) ] = -1.0;
	}
}

const ncv = 6;
const ldv = n;
const V = new Float64Array( ldv * ncv );
const resid = new Float64Array( n );
for ( i = 0; i < n; i++ ) {
	resid[ i ] = 1.0 + ( 0.1 * ( i + 1 ) );
}
const workd = new Float64Array( 3 * n );
const lworkl = ( ncv * ncv ) + ( 8 * ncv );
const workl = new Float64Array( lworkl );
const iparam = new Int32Array( 11 );
iparam[ 0 ] = 1; // exact shifts
iparam[ 2 ] = 100; // max iterations
iparam[ 6 ] = 1; // mode 1
const ipntr = new Int32Array( 11 );
const ido = new Int32Array( 1 );
const state = {};

// Reverse-communication loop; info=1 signals a user-supplied initial residual.
let info = 1;
let p, q, r, c, acc;
do {
	info = dsaupd( 'column-major', state, ido, 'standard', n, 'LM', 3, 0.0, resid, 1, ncv, V, ldv, iparam, 1, ipntr, 1, workd, workl, lworkl, info );
	if ( ido[ 0 ] === -1 || ido[ 0 ] === 1 ) {
		p = ipntr[ 0 ];
		q = ipntr[ 1 ];
		for ( r = 0; r < n; r++ ) {
			acc = 0.0;
			for ( c = 0; c < n; c++ ) {
				acc += A[ r + ( c * n ) ] * workd[ p + c ];
			}
			workd[ q + r ] = acc;
		}
	}
} while ( ido[ 0 ] !== 99 );

console.log( 'info: %d, iterations: %d, converged: %d', info, iparam[ 2 ], iparam[ 4 ] ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'largest Ritz values:', [ workl[ ipntr[ 5 ] - 1 ], workl[ ipntr[ 5 ] ], workl[ ipntr[ 5 ] + 1 ] ] ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>
